sections.title: Diagnosis Summary
sections.content:
**Primary Risk: Communication & Confidence Risk.**

Communication and Overall Readiness are both **1.75/5**. Technical is **2.7/5**, Resume and Structure are both **3.2/5**, and Behavioural is **3.4/5**.

Aditya's resume gives him a concrete credit risk example to lead with. At R.K. Clearing, he built Excel cash flow and exposure models that monitored €2.4m in transaction volume and supported credit limit decisions for 40 commercial clients. In the first mock, ask him to explain one account review. Check whether the listener can identify the decision, the main risk signal and Aditya's own contribution after one hearing.

sections.title: Resume Evidence and Credibility Checks
sections.content:
### Define the three financial figures
The resume cites a €300k client portfolio, €2.4m in transaction volume and approximately €400k in exposure covered by weekly reports. Prepare the definition, period and source for each. Explain whether the figures cover overlapping clients and what each number measures.

### Establish ownership of the credit limit work
Choose one anonymised account. Explain which data you assembled, how you calculated exposure, what recommendation the analysis supported and who approved the decision. Clarify whether the 40-client figure covers all accounts monitored by the model or a specific review period.

### Verify the Sanden Vikas reporting claim
The resume reports dashboards tracking €6m in operating expenditure and saving about five hours per reporting cycle. Show what the previous process involved, what you changed and how you estimated the saving. Keep this example separate from the academic variance dashboard, which used simulated data.

sections.title: How Communication Risk May Show Up
sections.content:
### The recommendation comes late
An interviewer asks what you recommended for a client whose exposure was rising. Start with the decision your analysis supported, then give the evidence that mattered most. Keep spreadsheet mechanics ready for follow-up.

### A challenge to the numbers derails the answer
When asked whether €2.4m was exposure or transaction volume, define the measure, give the period and explain how it relates to the account under discussion. Practise answering this in two sentences before adding detail.

### The explanation stays the same for every audience
A risk analyst may ask for the calculation and reconciliation. Senior leadership may ask about the implication and what action is needed. Practise both versions and ask the listener what they understood. Use the mock to establish whether the gap is in delivery, answer structure or technical reasoning.

sections.title: Priority Fix Order

steps.title: Establish a baseline and verify the figures
steps.content: Record a 60-second introduction and a 90-second account review. Ask the listener to repeat the recommendation, evidence and your role. Verify the definitions and periods behind the three R.K. Clearing figures.

steps.title: Practise a clear exposure model walkthrough
steps.content: Reconstruct one anonymised Excel example. Explain the inputs, calculation, limit comparison and reconciliation. Identify one assumption that could change the recommendation.

steps.title: Adapt the same finding to two audiences
steps.content: Explain a slower-collections scenario to a risk analyst and to senior leadership. Give the technical drivers in one version and the cash impact and next action in the other. Answer two follow-up questions.

steps.title: Run a role-specific mock and reassess
steps.content: Use a Credit Risk Analyst job description. Repeat the baseline question, add a liquidity scenario and use one real behavioural example about a challenged analysis. Compare the two recordings using the same rubric.

sections.content: Use one real example each week. Keep the first and final recordings so the candidate and mentor can compare responses to the same prompt.

sections.title: Resume-Anchored Technical Preparation
sections.content:
### R.K. Clearing exposure and limit monitoring
Walk through one account from transaction records to the exposure calculation and limit comparison. Explain how you checked the inputs, which signal triggered review and what evidence would change the recommendation.

### R.K. Clearing liquidity and working capital
Explain how days sales outstanding, days payable outstanding and the cash conversion cycle informed the rolling forecast. Practise a case where collections slow. Identify which assumptions change, the effect on forecast cash and the action you would flag to leadership.

### Sanden Vikas variance and dashboard reporting
Choose one variance from the operating expenditure dashboard. Explain the source, how you checked the data and how you investigated the driver. If discussing the academic dashboard, explain how you used Power Query, SUMIFS and dynamic flags on simulated data.

### Trinity College Dublin dissertation
Explain the research question on capital buffers and solvency at global systemically important banks. Prepare the sample, stress periods, panel approach and one limitation. Practise giving the finding in plain language before describing the method.

sections.title: Interview Answer Construction Guidance
sections.content:
**Practice question:** How did your Excel model support a credit limit decision at R.K. Clearing?

**Before:** “I built an Excel model to monitor transactions and help set credit limits.”

**After:** “In one commercial account review, my analysis supported [verified recommendation]. I calculated exposure from [inputs] and compared it with [approved limit]. The main risk signal was [finding]. I reconciled the result against [source] and shared my recommendation with [decision owner]. The next indicator I monitored was [indicator].”

Use an actual anonymised account to fill in the details. The revised answer gives the interviewer a decision to understand, a calculation to probe and a clear account of your contribution.

sections.title: High-Priority Interview Questions
sections.content:
1. What did the €300k portfolio, €2.4m transaction volume and approximately €400k reported exposure each measure?
2. Walk through one Excel exposure calculation. Which inputs drove the result and how did you reconcile them?
3. For one of the 40 commercial clients, what would make you recommend lowering, maintaining or increasing the credit limit? Who approved the decision?
4. If days sales outstanding rose, how would your rolling cash forecast change and what would you flag to leadership?
5. Describe a forecast-versus-actual variance you investigated at R.K. Clearing. How did you validate the driver and communicate it?
6. How did you estimate the five-hour reporting saving at Sanden Vikas?
7. What did your MSc dissertation find about capital buffers and solvency, and what limitation affects how the finding can be interpreted?
8. Tell me about a stakeholder who challenged your analysis. What did you check, how did you respond and what happened?

data.label: Session 1: Baseline communication
data.objective: Record the introduction and account review. Check whether the listener can identify the recommendation, evidence and Aditya's role.

data.label: Session 2: Technical depth
data.objective: Probe the exposure calculation, limit comparison, reconciliation and one assumption that would change the recommendation.

data.label: Session 3: Liquidity and stakeholder reporting
data.objective: Explain a slower-collections scenario to a risk analyst and a senior stakeholder. Practise responding to a challenge to the forecast.

data.label: Session 4: Role-specific simulation
data.objective: Use a real vacancy, repeat the baseline question and test one technical scenario and one behavioural example.

sections.content: After each session, record what the listener understood, which follow-up exposed a gap and one action to practise before the next mock.

sections.title: Expected Outcome and How to Use This Plan

candidateSteps.title: Verify the financial figures
candidateSteps.content: Define the period, source and scope of each major resume figure. Prepare an anonymised account example and identify your own contribution.

candidateSteps.title: Prepare three role-specific walkthroughs
candidateSteps.content: Rehearse one credit limit recommendation, one liquidity forecast and one variance investigation. Give the decision or finding in the opening sentence.

candidateSteps.title: Practise adapting to the audience
candidateSteps.content: Explain one risk finding to a risk analyst and to senior leadership. Answer two follow-up questions and use the feedback to revise the answer.

mentorSteps.title: Test the reported communication risk
mentorSteps.content: Prioritise Communication 1.75 and Overall Readiness 1.75. Observe whether Aditya answers directly, explains ownership and responds clearly when challenged.

mentorSteps.title: Keep assessment scores distinct
mentorSteps.content: Keep Technical 2.7 separate from Communication 1.75. Probe calculation, validation and assumptions. The separate Technical Readiness Score was blank.

mentorSteps.title: Reassess with evidence
mentorSteps.content: Repeat the baseline prompt. Check whether the listener can identify the recommendation, its rationale, Aditya's role and the next action.

sections.content:
**Desired outcome:** Aditya can state a credit risk recommendation early, support it with a defensible calculation and explain what would change his view.

**Completion checks:** A concise introduction, an anonymised exposure walkthrough, a working capital scenario, a clear dissertation explanation and one real behavioural example about communicating a disputed finding.
